kicker: Gaussian splats inside a BIM/CIM cloud

scenes.headline: How a BIM cloud measures on Gaussian splats
scenes.sub: Volumes, sections and alignment on blobs that are not a surface
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Thepla! A construction cloud now puts Gaussian splat scans beside building models. Here is what measuring on them takes.

scenes.text: A splat is millions of soft, translucent blobs trained to match photos. Every measurement must first decide where the surface is.
scenes.say: A splat is millions of soft blobs trained to match photos, not to sit on surfaces. So every measurement first decides where the surface is.

scenes.title: A Revit model inside a scan

steps.say: Here a Revit building stands inside a scanned plaza, in one shared space.
For that to mean anything, both need the same coordinates.
Video gives camera poses, with GPS as a weak hint, and the poses train the splat.
Surveyed targets pin it down. Three is the minimum, so put out five and keep two as checks.
The Revit model joins through its shared coordinates, exported to I F C with a map conversion.

steps.say: This is the product's own volume tool, on a half-metre grid over a staircase.
Fill and cut are read straight off the splat. The reference surface is not stated.

items.say: A height offset between epochs is area times offset, and it never averages out.
A tilt can net to zero, but it still inflates cut and fill separately.
Floaters and trees add fake fill, unless a median takes them out.

scenes.label: as-built accuracy Japan's rules require, proven with check points
scenes.say: Japan's rules want plus or minus fifty millimetres for as-built work, proven on check points. The splat path publishes no accuracy figure.

scenes.text: Use the splat to show the site. Take geometry from whatever measured it.
scenes.say: So use the splat to show the site, and take geometry from whatever actually measured it.

recap: A splat is not a surface
Align on targets, check on more
scenes.say: Splats are not surfaces. Align on targets and check on more. And measure volumes on a surface you trust.
